title: Using Motoko Hashmaps to Store Token Balances
summary: Builds the token's backend ledger in Motoko: an owner Principal, total supply and symbol, a HashMap from Principal to Nat holding balances, and a balanceOf query that safely unwraps the optional returned by get. Finishes by deploying and calling balanceOf from the command line.

concepts.heading: Principal: identifying users and canisters
points: Principal is the Internet Computer type that uniquely identifies either a user (identity) or a canister.
Get your own id as text with dfx identity get-principal; it is a long dash-separated string for the default identity.
Import the type (import Principal from mo:base/Principal). Principal.fromText converts that string into a real Principal value; a plain Text cannot be used where a Principal is required.
The owner is the identity that receives the entire initial supply when the canister is created.

concepts.heading: Actor state: owner, totalSupply, symbol
points: Create an actor named Token in main.mo and define its variables inside it.
owner : Principal, assigned via Principal.fromText with your own id pasted in (whole string, all dashes).
totalSupply : Nat, set to one billion (nine zeros). Nat is a natural number, so it can never be negative.
symbol : Text, the short ticker (DANG here). Tickers imitate currency codes such as USD, GBP or ETH; the learner may choose any name.

(Extra) Newer reference code writes these as persistent actor with transient var, which is the Motoko enhanced-orthogonal-persistence syntax; the lecture uses a plain actor and var/let, and either way the ledger in this lesson is not meant to survive upgrades (that is handled in a later lesson).

concepts.heading: The ledger as a HashMap
points: A ledger here is a store mapping an account id to the amount of tokens it holds. A dictionary-like structure fits, and Motoko's version is HashMap (a hash table): a key is hashed to find where its value lives, so lookups are efficient.
Import it with import HashMap from mo:base/HashMap (watch the capitals).
Declare: var balances = HashMap.HashMap<Principal, Nat>(1, Principal.equal, Principal.hash). The generic arguments are key type then value type.
Constructor arguments: (1) initial capacity, here 1; (2) an equality function so the map can compare keys, Principal.equal; (3) a hash function for the key type, Principal.hash.

balances.put(key, value) inserts a value at a key and overwrites any previous entry for that key. Calling balances.put(owner, totalSupply) at the top level of the actor gives the owner the whole supply when the canister is installed.

concepts.heading: balanceOf query function
points: public query func balanceOf(who : Principal) : async Nat. query means it reads state only and returns fast without going through consensus; async because all public canister functions return a future.
balances.get(who) returns an Option: ?Nat. If the key is absent the result is null, not a number, so it cannot be returned directly as Nat.
An Option is a type-safe null: it keeps the underlying type but allows 'no value'. It is the same idea as Swift optionals.

Unwrap with switch: switch (balances.get(who)) { case null 0; case (?result) result }. The null branch yields 0 (account has no balance); the ?result branch binds the inner Nat to result and drops the question mark.
Assign the switch result to let balance : Nat and return it. The earlier if-null-then-0 approach becomes unnecessary.

concepts.heading: Deploying and calling from the CLI
points: Save main.mo then run dfx deploy again; the canister is reinstalled with the owner holding the full supply.
Candid arguments on the command line must be typed: a Principal argument has to look like principal "id", not just the id text.
Build that string once in a shell variable using command substitution, check it with echo, then call the method with dfx canister call token balanceOf and the variable.

The response shows the billion as a nat, confirming the ledger and balanceOf work. The starter project's README holds copy-paste versions of these commands to avoid typos, plus a place to save your own principal for later lessons.

code_examples.caption: main.mo after this lesson (reconstructed; reference repo uses persistent actor + transient var)
CLI sequence to deploy and check the owner balance
code_examples.code:
dfx identity get-principal            # prints your principal id (text)
dfx deploy                            # redeploy after editing main.mo
OWNER_PUBLIC_KEY="principal \"$(dfx identity get-principal)\""
echo $OWNER_PUBLIC_KEY                # principal "xxxxx-...-xxx"
dfx canister call token balanceOf "$OWNER_PUBLIC_KEY"   # (1_000_000_000 : nat)

task.name: Create the ledger and check the owner's balance
task.starting_point: The skeleton project from the previous lesson with an empty main.mo.
task.goal: Mint a total supply to your own principal in a HashMap ledger and read it back through a balanceOf query.
steps: Run dfx identity get-principal and copy the id.
In main.mo import Principal and HashMap, then define actor Token.
Add owner (Principal.fromText with your id), totalSupply (Nat, 1 billion) and symbol (Text).
Create balances as a HashMap<Principal, Nat> with initial size 1, Principal.equal and Principal.hash.
Put the owner into balances with the full total supply.
Write public query func balanceOf(who : Principal) : async Nat that switches on balances.get(who): null gives 0, ?result gives result.
In the terminal create OWNER_PUBLIC_KEY in the principal "id" format, echo it, then dfx canister call token balanceOf with it.
task.expected_result: The canister call returns 1_000_000_000 : nat for the owner principal.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 41 - Create Your Own Crypto Token/41.03 Using Motoko Hashmaps to Store Token Balances/DANG/src/DANG_backend/main.mo

pitfalls: Passing the principal as plain text to balanceOf: it must be wrapped as principal "...".
Forgetting to import HashMap or Principal, or mistyping the capitals.
Trying to return balances.get(who) directly: it is ?Nat, not Nat.
Copying only part of the principal string into fromText.

(Extra) The reference README sets OWNER_PUBLIC_KEY with single quotes, which stops $(...) from expanding in a shell; use double quotes with escaped inner quotes as in the CLI snippet. Also the correct command spelling is dfx identity get-principal (the README text shows a stray 'get -principal').
(Extra) The reference repo's hard-coded principal is the student's own; use yours.

gaps_and_ideas: Proposed lesson 'Token ledger with a HashMap': blurb on mapping principals to balances and Option unwrapping. Tasks: (1) declare owner/totalSupply/symbol, (2) create balances HashMap with the 3 constructor args, (3) put the owner entry, (4) write balanceOf with switch on null/?result, (5) call balanceOf for the owner and for an unknown principal (expect 0).
Starter code idea: main.mo with TODO comments and a stubbed balanceOf returning 0.
Interactive demo idea: a JS mock ledger (Map) where users call get() and see the null branch vs the value branch, with a visual of key hashing into buckets.
